_comment: Human corrections to parser attribution, keyed by the clip id the parser produced.
This is the review step: the parser never guesses silently, and anything it cannot
resolve is pinned here by a person.
A clip id is a hash of (speaker + spoken text), so it is stable against paragraph
insertion. When a segment is pinned to a different speaker its final clip id changes
to match the corrected speaker; that is intended, because a different voice is a
different clip.
Each entry may set:
speaker  - the correct speaker id from story-rules/voice-registry.json
ttsText  - a pronunciation-only rewrite; displayText stays canonical
note     - why
Run `python3 scripts/audio.py validate` to see what still needs pinning.
ONE FAILURE KEEPS RECURRING, AND IT IS WORTH NAMING. Every correction below after
the first is the same sentence shape: an action beat that names Jack as the OWNER
or the ANSWERER of a device, immediately before a line spoken by whoever is on the
other end of it. 'Jack's wrist terminal chirped again.' 'Jack answered, and Lena's
voice burst through it.' 'Behind him, Sarah had walked toward a window.' The
nearest name is not the speaker in any of them -- it is the listener, or the thing
the speaker is arriving through. The parser reads the nearest named person as the
speaker, which is right most of the time and exactly wrong here.

REVIEW_REQUIRED-28f9c13a10b8.speaker: jack-bennett
REVIEW_REQUIRED-28f9c13a10b8.note: Chapter 1, paragraph 26: 'Jack released the intercom and looked back at the monitor. The TOMBS directory was still open. "Who are you?"' Jack is the actor of the paragraph; the parser could not see it because the sentence immediately before the quote is about the directory rather than about a person. Reviewed against the manuscript 2026-09-17.

jack-bennett-90d6c9b3d753.note: Chapter 2: 'Jack's wrist terminal chirped again. "Jack? We disconnected you."' The terminal is Jack's; the voice coming out of it is Lena's, answering the disconnect she was asked for two lines earlier and which she confirmed with 'Doing it now.' Jack cannot be asking himself whether he is Jack. Caught by Joshua on the audio, 2026-09-20.

jack-bennett-2a675d4ecfca.note: Chapter 3: 'His wrist terminal chirped with an incoming call from island utility control. Jack answered, and Lena's voice burst through it. "Jack! Jack, answer me!"' The manuscript names the speaker in the same sentence -- Lena's voice -- and the parser still took Jack, because Jack is the one who ANSWERED. Found auditing chapters 2 and 3 after Joshua caught the chapter 2 one, 2026-09-20.

jack-bennett-bd45d3e4f5ac.speaker: sarah-bennett
jack-bennett-bd45d3e4f5ac.note: Chapter 3: 'Behind him, Sarah had walked toward a window. "Jack."' She is calling him; he is the name being said, not the one saying it. The line four segments later -- 'Sarah called again from the window. "Jack."' -- was attributed to Sarah correctly, which is what made this one visible: the same word from the same woman twice, once in the wrong voice. Found auditing chapters 2 and 3, 2026-09-20. SCOPED TO CHAPTERS 3 AND 6 on 2026-09-21: the revised Chapter 6 has Sarah say 'Jack.' again in the same shape, and until the scoping existed this one pin was quietly firing in both places. It is right in both, but it was right by luck.
